facts.fact: The town bought the Colburn farm in 1899 to protect its watershed; the Water Commissioners' certificate of 28 March 1923 made it the club's land, leased from the town ever since.
OSM tags the course land owner=Town Of Needham, protected=perpetuity.
Designed by Wayne Stiles; the 2026 scorecard says 'A Wayne Stiles Design', 1923.
The club's own logo is two pine trees with a red flag; this logo avoids pines and flags.

concepts.name: The Town Pump
concepts.rationale: The course is the town's watershed land: a red cast-iron pitcher pump on a granite plinth, a drop of water falling from its spout.
references: Town watershed land, 1899; Water Commissioners' certificate, 1923 (facts)
concepts.symbolism: Town water, town land, a club that started with a water board's certificate.
concepts.interpretation: The pump itself is an interpretation: no pump on the course is claimed.
concepts.strengths: A single bold object, red on the green course card; reads at 1x.
concepts.tradeoffs: The watershed story needs telling; a golfer won't guess it from the pump.

recommendation: Concept 1 (course chat, overnight 2026-10-31; the developer may change it).
